rv.q: Trap Door delivers a substantial piece of theater that is at once pungent social commentary and delightful entertainment.
In this regard, “Princess Ivona” is successful.
Laura Nelson gives a star performance, not exaggerated or self-pitying, but simply allowing Ivona to have naturalistic reactions to the ridiculous people surrounding her.

cn.t: Trap Door Theatre's lean adaptation of Gombrowicz's absurdist satire wins praise for its daring, immersive production in an intimate space, though the show's challenging absurdist style may not connect with all audiences.
